entities.label: Institution
entities.summary: Saint Gregory of Nyssa was a church and monastery of Trabzon. It's believed the church was built around 1280-1297 by the wife of John III, Emperor of Trabzon. After 1665, St Gregory became the cathedral of the city of Trabzon. The church is dedicated to Saint Gregory of Nyssa, a Christian bishop and saint. Nyssa is a city located in Cappadocia. Georgian traveler Timote Gabashvili visited the church in the late 1750s and included this event in his writings. In 1863, the Metropolitan Constantius of Trabzon rebuilt the church. Saint Gregory of Nyssa Church, Trabzon is a church building in Asia, established in 1201. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Saint Gregory of Nyssa Church in Trabzon played a significant role in regional Christian heritage and architecture, particularly during the Ottoman period. Its rebuilding by Metropolitan Constantius in 1863 helped preserve its historical significance.
